summary: Neyveli Uttar Pradesh Power Limited, KH-419, G.N. Extension, Gomti Nagar, Lucknow - 226010, Uttar Pradesh ** Petitioner** 5. The Petitioner vide affidavit dated 29.1.2025, has filed this petition in accordance with Regulation 9(1) and Regulation 10 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, after serving a copy of the same on the Respondents. Accordingly, the annual fixed charges claimed by the Petitioner, are as under: 6. The Petitioner has also prayed for the grant of an interim tariff, equivalent to 85% of the total tariff claimed for billing purposes, subject to the final determination of the tariff. 7. During the hearing of the petition on 8.4.2025, the learned counsel for the Petitioner made oral submissions and prayed that the Commission may grant an interim tariff to the Petitioner at 80% (subsequently revised as 85% by the learned counsel) of the total tariff claimed, in terms of Regulations 9 and 10 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, as it has furnished all the information. The learned counsel for the Respondent UPPCL accepted the notice and requested time to file its reply in the matter. However, the learned counsel for the Petitioner clarified that since the interim tariff has been prayed for by the Petitioner (which is subject to final determination), the Respondent may be directed to file its reply on the said prayer at this stage. This request was accepted by the Commission. Accordingly, the Commission directed the Respondents to file their replies after serving a copy to the Petitioner. The Petitioner has also published the tariff petition in terms of Regulation 23(7) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations. 2023. Reply to the petition, limited to the question of the grant of interim tariff to the generating station, has been filed by the Respondent, UPPCL vide affidavit dated 2.5.2025 8. The Commission, after hearing the learned counsel for the parties, reserved its orders with regard to the prayer of the Petitioner for the grant of an interim tariff in respect of Unit-I of the generating station, in terms of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. 9. In order to enable the Petitioner to meet its ongoing financial obligations through a reasonable recovery of the cost of supply of electricity by the Petitioner to the Respondents and keeping in view that the interim tariff of the generating station will be subject to adjustment, based on the final tariff to be determined by the Commission, we, on prudence check, proceed to examine the prayer of the Petitioner for the grant of interim tariff in this petition, as stated in the subsequent paragraphs. 10. Some of the provisions of Regulation 9(1) and Regulation 10(3) of the 2024 Tariff _(3) If the information furnished in the petition is in accordance with these regulations, the Commission may consider granting an interim tariff of up to ninety per cent (90%) of the tariff claimed in the case of a new generating station or unit thereof or transmission system, or element thereof during the first hearing of the application for billing purposes till the final tariff is determined by the Commission:_ 12. The Respondent UPPCL has submitted that the Petitioner has not complied with the requirement to furnish the statutory auditor’s certificate within a period of 90 days from 14. The Petitioner has furnished the reasons for the delay of 1477 days in the commissioning of Unit-I, viz., delay due to land acquisition and delay due to other issues and has submitted that these were beyond the control of the Petitioner. The Respondent has submitted that the Petitioner's claim for IDC and IEDC is fundamentally defective as it fails to comply with the mandatory requirements of Regulation 21(3) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations read with Form-F of Appendix-I, which expressly requires the generating company to submit detailed particulars and documentary evidence substantiating the specific cost overruns incurred. It has been stated that such material omission of the Petitioner has rendered its IDC/IEDC claims wholly unsubstantiated and legally untenable under the 2024 Tariff Regulations. Since the question of time overrun and cost overrun involved in the project is required to be decided after a detailed hearing of the parties, at the time of determination of the final tariff of the generating station, the same is not considered in this order. 19. The operational norms claimed by the Petitioner in terms of provisions of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, which are considered as under: 24. The interim tariff granted as above is subject to adjustment based on the determination of the final tariff of Unit-I from its COD till 31.3.2029, in terms of the provisions of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. Also, as stated earlier, the interim tariff granted for Unit-I shall be in operation for the period till 31.3.2027 or till the determination of the final tariff, whichever is earlier. _Order in Petition No. 370/GT/2025 Page_ **_13_** _of_ **13** CERC Website S. title: Petition under Sections 62 and 79 (1) (a) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 9(1) and 10 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024 for determination of tariff for the Ghatampur Thermal Power Station (1980 MW) of Neyveli Uttar Pradesh Power Limited from the date of COD of Unit-I (i.e., 12.12.2024) till 31.3.2029.
